Your digital product checkout is more than a payment button. 👀 If you sell ebooks, templates, courses, guides, Canva templates, or other digital products, you need to think about what happens after someone clicks “buy.” Before selling your first digital product, make sure you have: 1️⃣ Purchase terms — what the customer is actually agreeing to when they buy. 2️⃣ License & use restrictions — what they can and cannot do with your product. 3️⃣ Privacy Policy — especially if you’re collecting customer information. 4️⃣ Website/store terms — the rules governing purchases and use of your store. 5️⃣ Protection against unauthorized sharing & reselling — because your digital product should not become the internet’s free download. 😭 Your creativity is an asset. Treat it like one. And remember: your legal protection shouldn’t start after someone steals or misuses your digital product. It should be part of your business from the beginning. The fastest way I know to find a digital product people will pay for is to read the bad reviews on ones that already sell. Step 1: find something that's already selling to the people you want to help. Look on Amazon or Etsy for planners, guides or checklists with lots of reviews. Step 2: read the worst reviews, the 1 and 2 stars, and copy each complaint into a list word for word. After about 20, the same complaint keeps coming up, and that's the one you want. Step 3: make the digital product that fixes that one complaint, and say it in the very first line of the page. The buyers have already told you what was missing, in public.
